summary: SUM, AVG, MIN, and MAX summarise many values into one.
points: They all ignore NULLs. AVG divides by the number of non-NULL values, not by all rows.
With no matching rows, SUM, AVG, MIN, and MAX return NULL, and COUNT returns 0.
AVG always returns a decimal, so wrap it in ROUND when needed.
MIN and MAX also work on text and dates.

example.sql:
SELECT SUM(bonus) AS total, AVG(bonus) AS average, MIN(hire_date) AS first_hire, MAX(salary) AS top_salary
FROM employees;
example.explanation: AVG(bonus) averages only the employees who have a recorded bonus.
